prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose first temple was dedicated before 1960.
prompts.text_original: Pin a country whose first temple of the Church was dedicated before 1960.
prompts.summary: For most of its history the Church's temples stood in the United States, with St. George, Utah (1877) the oldest still on the list. Before 1960 only four other countries had one: Canada (Cardston, 1923), Switzerland (near Bern, 1955, the first in Europe), and New Zealand and the United Kingdom (both 1958).

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: St. George, 1877.

answers.name: Canada
answers.fact: Cardston, Alberta, 1923.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Near Bern, 1955, the first in Europe.

answers.name: United Kingdom
answers.fact: London, near Lingfield, 1958.

answers.name: New Zealand
answers.fact: Hamilton, 1958.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in Jeremiah 39-44, from Jerusalem's fall to the flight into Egypt
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place in Jeremiah 39-44, from the fall of Jerusalem to the flight into Egypt: Zedekiah judged at Riblah, captives taken to Babylon, Jeremiah freed at Ramah, Gedaliah at Mizpah, Ishmael's flight to the Ammonites, and the remnant's settlements at Tahpanhes and Pathros
prompts.note: Ramah, Mizpah and Gibeon are in the West Bank (Palestine). Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts.
prompts.summary: After Babylon broke into Jerusalem, Zedekiah was blinded at Riblah and taken to Babylon. Jeremiah, freed at Ramah, stayed with the governor Gedaliah at Mizpah until Ishmael, sent by the Ammonite king, murdered him. Fearing Babylon, the remnant fled to Egypt and took Jeremiah with them to Tahpanhes (Jer 39-44).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Against Jeremiah's word the remnant went to Tahpanhes, and Jews dwelt at Migdol, Noph and Pathros (Jer 43:7; 44:1).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Zedekiah was bound and carried to Babylon, with the rest of the people (Jer 39:7-9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem was broken up in Zedekiah's eleventh year (Jer 39:2).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Zedekiah was overtaken in the plains of Jericho, and mourners came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria; Jeremiah was loosed at Ramah and went to Gedaliah at Mizpah (Jer 39:5; 40:1, 6; 41:5).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Baalis king of the Ammonites sent Ishmael to slay Gedaliah, and Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites (Jer 40:14; 41:15); Jews returned from Moab, Ammon and Edom to Gedaliah (Jer 40:11).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Nebuchadrezzar judged Zedekiah at Riblah in the land of Hamath (Jer 39:5).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding one of Rehoboam's fenced cities, or a homeland of Shishak's army
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding one of Rehoboam's fenced cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:5-10) or the homeland of a people in Shishak's army that came against him (2 Chronicles 12:2-3: Egyptians, Lubims, and the people of Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt)
prompts.note: Cush lay mostly in Sudan, reaching into southern Egypt; Ethiopia does not count. Bethlehem, Tekoa and Hebron are in the West Bank.
prompts.summary: After the kingdom split, Rehoboam built a ring of fenced cities to guard Judah, from Bethlehem and Hebron to Lachish and Aijalon. Because Judah forsook the law, Shishak of Egypt came with chariots and a host of Lubims, Sukkiims and Ethiopians, took the fenced cities and carried off the temple treasures (2 Chr 11-12).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year (2 Chr 12:2).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Rehoboam fortified Lachish, Azekah, Adullam, Gath, Zorah and Aijalon (2 Chr 11:7-10).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: He also fortified Bethlehem, Tekoa, Beth-zur and Hebron (2 Chr 11:6-10).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: The Lubims marched with Shishak (2 Chr 12:3); the Church footnote reads Libyans, and BD Libya is the land west of Egypt.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: The Ethiopians marched with him too (2 Chr 12:3); Bible Ethiopia was the Nile land south of Egypt.

prompts.display_text: Pin a Latin American mainland country whose first stake (a group of congregations) was organized 1977-1979
prompts.text_original: Stakes spread quickly through Latin America in the late 1970s. A country in Mexico, Central America or Spanish- or Portuguese-speaking South America whose first stake was organized from 1977 through 1979.
prompts.summary: In just three years eight Latin American countries got their first stakes, from San Jose and Bogota in January 1977 to Panama City in November 1979. Earlier firsts came in Mexico, Brazil, Argentina, Guatemala, Uruguay, Peru, Chile and El Salvador; Nicaragua followed in 1981, and Belize still has a district.

answers.name: Colombia
answers.fact: Bogota Colombia Stake, January 23, 1977.

answers.name: Ecuador
answers.fact: Guayaquil, June 4, 1978, the first stake in Ecuador.

answers.name: Venezuela
answers.fact: Caracas Venezuela Stake, May 15, 1977.

answers.name: Bolivia
answers.fact: Santa Cruz Bolivia Stake, January 14, 1979.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: San Jose Costa Rica Stake, January 20, 1977.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: San Pedro Sula Honduras Stake, April 10, 1977.

answers.name: Paraguay
answers.fact: Asuncion Paraguay Stake, February 25, 1979.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: Panama Stake, November 11, 1979.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where US servicemen held the first Church meetings or were the first members (before 1955).
prompts.text_original: In several places the Church took root not through missionaries but through Latter-day Saints serving in the United States military, who were the first known members or held the first Church meetings there. Pin a country or territory where the Global Histories record this happening before 1955.
prompts.summary: Before formal missions arrived, Latter-day Saints in the US military often became the Church's first presence in a land. Two soldiers held the first service in Manila in 1898, and in World War II and after, servicemen's groups met in Costa Rica, Guam, New Guinea, the Marshall Islands, Puerto Rico, Korea and the Azores.

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: First Church meetings in Korea held by US servicemen, 1945-47.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Soldiers George Seaman and Willard Call held the first service in Manila, August 21, 1898.

answers.name: Guam
answers.fact: First members on Guam were with the US military, 1944-46.

answers.name: Puerto Rico
answers.fact: Servicemen met in homes in the 1940s; 1953 meetings at Fort Buchanan chapel.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: First members in Costa Rica were US servicemen, July 1944.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: Servicemen held services in New Guinea, 1944-45.

answers.name: Marshall Islands
answers.fact: First Church services held by American military personnel in the 1940s.

answers.name: Portugal
answers.fact: Earliest known members were servicemen at Lajes Field, Azores, in the 1950s.
